title: GameControls
responsibility: Display level-specific player status and touch movement controls while preserving legacy key-door branches.

inputs.name: GameControls.view
inputs.description: The level or legacy key-door view being played; this component reads only its `world`. When `world` is set (a built level) it shows the four directional buttons and hides the key and door chips and the Garden and Vault buttons; without it, it shows the left and right buttons, the key and door chips, and the Garden and Vault buttons.

inputs.name: GameControls.run
inputs.description: The current run: this component reads `state.x` and `state.y` (shown to two decimals), `state.outcome` (shown when truthy), and, outside a built level, `state.hasKey` and `state.doorOpen` for the key and door chips and to enable the Garden and Vault buttons. Any `x` or `y` that `Number()` reads as NaN, including a missing one, displays as NaN, and no other run field is read.

inputs.name: GameControls.step
inputs.description: Called once per button click with a GameInput: a direction button sends `{ x, y }` with one axis at -1 or 1 and the other at 0 (up is y -1, down is y 1, left is x -1, right is x 1), and the Garden and Vault buttons send `{ x: 0, y: 0, choice }` with choice 'garden' or 'vault', but only while enabled, which means `state.doorOpen` is truthy. The component does not catch errors the callback throws.

inputs.name: GameControls.reset
inputs.description: Starts the run again where the view begins, as the types file documents; the component calls it only as the Reset button's click handler, so it is called with the click event. The Reset button is shown in every mode, including a built level.

outputs.name: GameControls
outputs.description: The component's markup: an x and y chip (two decimals), Key and Door chips outside a built level, a Reached chip when the outcome is set, then the movement buttons (four in a built level, left and right otherwise), the Garden and Vault buttons outside a built level, and Reset. The arrow-key hint is static text, since the component attaches no keyboard listeners.
